# Skills

Design criteria of Anima as skill documents for any AI coding agent. Load the one that matches the work before you start; `AGENTS.md` has the table that says which one for which paths.

Three families, one schema: `## Use this when`, `## Rules`, `## Questions to answer before proposing`, `## Where the result goes`, with the front matter `name`, `description`, `family` and `paths`. A product skill is named for a kind of work. A capability skill is named `anima-<capability>-design` and covers one directory of `engine/` or `config/`. A technology skill is named `anima-tech-<technology>`, records how that technology actually behaves, and is retired when the technology is replaced. A rule that nobody has seen working starts with `Unverified:`; the count per skill shows how much is still to be shown.

## Product skills

- [`anima-adopting-a-component`](anima-adopting-a-component.md) (1 unverified): Use when adding, replacing or evaluating a tool, library, service, GitHub Action, image or test suite for Anima, or when tempted to write a script of our own: order of preference, evaluation facts, fork and pinning mechanics, gaps.toml.
- [`anima-branching-and-releasing`](anima-branching-and-releasing.md) (2 unverified): Use when opening or merging a pull request, changing CI or the promotion workflow, moving main-green, preparing or publishing a release, or choosing a version number: trunk-based development, the two tiers of verification, build once and promote, Semantic Versioning.
- [`anima-designing-a-port`](anima-designing-a-port.md) (1 unverified): Use when adding a capability to Anima, choosing or replacing the product that provides one, or deciding what the engine contains and whether something is an adapter: ports, adapters, state, circular dependencies.
- [`anima-designing-for-production`](anima-designing-for-production.md) (3 unverified): Use when designing anything that touches a running Anima installation (first start, upgrade, configuration, backup, data, start order, readiness, the engine image) or writing the engine's units or anything under engine/ or config/.
- [`anima-licensing-and-brand`](anima-licensing-and-brand.md) (2 unverified): Use when adding a component with a licence, accepting a contribution, naming something public, or writing about hosting and the marks: the AGPL with dual licensing, the contributor agreement, the plugin exception, the trademarks and the policy for using them.
- [`anima-maintaining-a-fork`](anima-maintaining-a-fork.md) (1 unverified): Use when touching anything under third_party/, moving a pin, adding a fork as a submodule, syncing a fork with upstream, or preparing a contribution upstream: mirror branches, the anima/<line> branch, merging and never rebasing, the sync workflow.
- [`anima-product-principles`](anima-product-principles.md) (0 unverified): Use when taking or proposing any design decision on Anima, reviewing a proposal or ADR, or choosing between options, for any component: the product-wide criteria and the checklist of questions before proposing.
- [`anima-repository-conventions`](anima-repository-conventions.md) (2 unverified): Use when adding or moving files in the anima repository, or changing mise tasks, git hooks, formatting, linting, REUSE annotations, caches, commit authorship, or when writing a decision record: layout, toolchain, generated files, the record format and tool.
- [`anima-specifying-requirements`](anima-specifying-requirements.md) (1 unverified): Use when adding or changing Anima behaviour, writing a requirement, verification or test, or touching model/anima.sysml, tests/ or tests/pending.toml: SysML v2 conventions, test naming, traceability.
- [`anima-working-as-an-agent`](anima-working-as-an-agent.md) (2 unverified): Use when planning, delegating, doing or reviewing work in the repository as an agent: the pipeline from task to promotion, the roles, the backlog, briefs and reports, postmortems, the catalog, the skill schema, the agent settings and the size limits.

## Capability skills

- [`anima-access-design`](anima-access-design.md) (1 unverified): Use when changing who can connect to the Anima database server and as what: roles, pg_hba.conf, scopes, tokens, access rules, the identity provider's wiring, the identities file, or anything under engine/access/ or config/access/.
- [`anima-configuration-design`](anima-configuration-design.md) (0 unverified): Use when touching anything under config/ or any setting the engine reads: what an adopter configures, defaults, profiles, the driver that selects an adapter, and where secrets are named.
- [`anima-database-design`](anima-database-design.md) (2 unverified): Use when changing the database server of Anima, the adapters that run inside its process (token validation, vector search, backup and restore) or anything under engine/database/, engine/backup/ or engine/vectors/.
- [`anima-image-design`](anima-image-design.md) (2 unverified): Use when changing the engine image: its container file, its Quadlet units, its start order and readiness target, how it is booted or run as a container, or anything under engine/image/.
- [`anima-secrets-design`](anima-secrets-design.md) (2 unverified): Use when changing anything about secrets, certificates, keys or unsealing: where a secret comes from, how it reaches its consumers, the secret store, the root of trust, or anything under engine/secrets/.

## Technology skills

- [`anima-tech-adrs-madr`](anima-tech-adrs-madr.md) (1 unverified): Use when writing, converting, checking or indexing decision records in Anima with MADR files and the adrs tool: required front matter, what adrs doctor does and does not check, the generated index, configuration that must not leak in from the user.
- [`anima-tech-backlog-md`](anima-tech-backlog-md.md) (1 unverified): Use when creating, editing or reading a task of the backlog in Anima with Backlog.md: installing the tool, its non-interactive commands, the task file format, which custom front matter keys and sections its commands keep, and what it must never do here (commit).
- [`anima-tech-github-governance`](anima-tech-github-governance.md) (1 unverified): Use when creating or changing rulesets, required status checks, the merge queue, GitHub Actions permissions, forks of upstream projects or workflows that commit or push in Anima's GitHub organization: what the platform accepts and refuses.
- [`anima-tech-keycloak`](anima-tech-keycloak.md) (1 unverified): Use when writing or debugging the identity provider in Anima with Keycloak: the issuer URL, granting a scope per user through realm roles, realm import, health checks in its image, its database password, test tokens, and why keycloak-config-cli was retired.
- [`anima-tech-mise`](anima-tech-mise.md) (1 unverified): Use when adding or changing a mise task, tool, git hook, lockfile entry, environment variable or dev container setting in Anima: file tasks, the github backend, npm and pipx lock material, parallel tasks sharing files, a user-level configuration leaking in, uv and Python.
- [`anima-tech-openbao`](anima-tech-openbao.md) (1 unverified): Use when writing or debugging the secret store in Anima with OpenBao: declarative self-initialization stanzas, the static seal and unattended unseal, Raft snapshots, the database secrets engine against PostgreSQL, the PKI engine, running the container unprivileged.
- [`anima-tech-opentofu`](anima-tech-opentofu.md) (1 unverified): Use when writing or debugging the configurator in Anima with OpenTofu and its PostgreSQL, secret-store and identity-provider providers: the unattended run, offline provider mirror, state in PostgreSQL, state encryption, write-only secrets, the adopter's identities file, stale state, destroy protection and the plan guard.
- [`anima-tech-podman-quadlet-bootc`](anima-tech-podman-quadlet-bootc.md) (2 unverified): Use when writing, building, validating or running the engine image in Anima with podman, Quadlet units and a bootc base: rootless builds, shipping inner images, running the image as a container, start order and readiness gating, static validation of units, health checks.
- [`anima-tech-postgresql-oauth`](anima-tech-postgresql-oauth.md) (3 unverified): Use when writing or debugging token logins, pg_hba.conf oauth rules, the pg_oidc_validator module, or a test client that connects with a bearer token, with PostgreSQL's oauth authentication and libpq in Anima: what the validator really checks, what the log says, how to build and configure it.
- [`anima-tech-sysml-pilot`](anima-tech-sysml-pilot.md) (1 unverified): Use when writing, validating or reading SysML v2 textual notation in Anima with the OMG Pilot Implementation: satisfy and verify references, thresholds with units, marking requirements with metadata, running the pilot as a checker, reading its JSON export.
- [`anima-tech-testcontainers-podman`](anima-tech-testcontainers-podman.md) (1 unverified): Use when writing or debugging a system test in Anima that starts containers with Testcontainers for Python on rootless podman: the API service, DOCKER_HOST, the reaper image, the socket path limit, cleanup.

Unverified rules in all skills: 36.

Globs of `paths` that match nothing yet, listed in `not-yet-present.toml` and in no other place: `engine/backup/**`, `engine/vectors/**`, `**/*.tf`, `third_party/opentofu/**`, `third_party/terraform-provider-postgresql/**`, `third_party/terraform-provider-vault/**`, `third_party/terraform-provider-keycloak/**`.

The content lives here, in plain Markdown with no vendor syntax. For Claude Code, `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is a thin pointer and `.claude/rules/<name>.md` names the skill to load for its paths; both are generated. Another agent vendor wires its own pointers the same way: create its native skill or rules entry, put the trigger description in it, and make it import or tell the agent to read `skills/<name>.md`, never copy the content.
